Rashi on Makkot 2b:10:1.hebrew: ומר סבר כופרא ממונא - שהזיק גופו של זה, ונתחייב ליורשיו דמי ההרוג:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:10:1.english: And one Sage holds that the ransom is monetary - For [the ox] damaged the body of this person, and [its owner] became obligated to [pay] his heirs the value of the one killed.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:11:1.hebrew: בדניזק שיימינן - בהכי הויא ליה כפרה כי יהיב דמי ניזק, ולקמיה מפרש טעמיה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:11:1.english: We assess in terms of the victim - In this way it is an atonement, when he gives the value of the victim; and later [the Gemara] explains its reasoning.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:1.hebrew: מאי טעמייהו דרבנן - דאילו ר' ישמעאל מסתבר טעמיה: כיון דכופרא כפרה, דמי עצמו בעי למיתב:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:1.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis? - For as for Rabbi Yishmael, his reasoning is logical: Since the ransom is an atonement, he must give the value of himself [i.e., the one who killed].

Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:2.hebrew: נאמר השתה למעלה - בנוגף אשה הרה: "כאשר ישית עליו בעל האשה" (שם):
Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:2.english: Imposition is stated above - with regard to one who strikes a pregnant woman: "As the husband of the woman shall impose upon him" (there).

Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:3.hebrew: ונאמר השתה למטה - בכופר, שנאמר "אם כופר יושת עליו":
Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:3.english: And imposition is stated below - With regard to ransom, as it is stated: "If ransom is imposed upon him."

Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:4.hebrew: מה להלן בדניזק - שמשלם דמי וולדות שנזוקו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:12:4.english: Just as there, [it is] in terms of the victim - For he pays the value of the fetuses that were harmed.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:13:1.hebrew: פדיון נפשו - משמע דנותן את הכופר:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:13:1.english: The redemption of his soul - This implies that he gives the ransom.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:13:2.hebrew: ורבנן - אמרי לך: אין, ודאי "פדיון נפשו" הוא, דכופרא כפרה. מיהו, בדניזק שיימינן, ובהכי הויא למזיק פדיון נפשו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:13:2.english: And the Rabbis - They would say to you: Yes, certainly it is "the redemption of his soul," for a ransom is an atonement. However, we assess [it] by [the value of] the victim, and in this way it constitutes the redemption of the soul of the one who caused the damage.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:14:1.hebrew: דאית ליה לדידיה - שיש לו לגנב ממון לשלם דמי הגניבה אם לא הוזמו, ולהם אין מה לשלם. דמיגו דאיהו לא הוה מזדבן, אם לא הוזמו, אינהו נמי כי הוזמו לא מזדבני, שהרי לא זממו למכרו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:14:1.english: That he has of his own - That the thief has money to pay the value of the theft, had [the witnesses] not been proven conspiring, whereas they have nothing to pay. For since he would not have been sold, had they not been proven conspiring, they too, when proven conspiring, are not sold, since they did not conspire to sell him:

Rashi on Makkot 2b:16:1.hebrew: וקנס אינו משלם ע"פ עצמו - דכתיב גבי כפל: ״אשר ירשיעון אלהים״ — פרט למרשיע את עצמו (ב"ק דף סד:):
Rashi on Makkot 2b:16:1.english: And one does not pay a fine based on his own admission - For it is written regarding the double payment: "Whom the judges shall condemn" (Exodus 22:8) — this excludes one who condemns himself (Bava Kamma 64b):

Rashi on Makkot 2b:16:2.hebrew: תדע - דקנסא הוא, שהרי המעידים בנפש לא הרגו אדם, ולא נהרג אדם על פיהם, ונהרגין ומשלמין ממון:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:16:2.english: Know - That it is a fine, for witnesses who testified about a capital matter did not kill anyone, and no one was executed on the basis of their testimony, and [nevertheless] they are executed and pay money.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל - עדים שלא הוזמו עד שנהרג הנדון ואח"כ הוזמו, אין נהרגין, כדאמרינן בפרקין (דף ה:): הרגו אין נהרגין, דכתיב: "כאשר זמם", ולא כאשר עשה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:1.english: And if one who stones is not stoned - Witnesses who were not rendered conspiring witnesses until the condemned man was executed, and afterward were rendered conspiring witnesses, are not executed, as we say in our chapter (5b): If they killed, they are not executed, for it is written: "as he conspired" — and not as he did.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:2.english: One who came to stone and did not stone - For he was rendered a conspiring witness before the accused was executed.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:1.hebrew: הוא שעשה מעשה במזיד אינו גולה - ההורג, שעשה מעשה, אם במזיד עשאו אינו גולה, ואפילו בזמן שאינו נהרג, כגון במזיד בלא התראה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:1.english: He, who performed an action, intentionally is not exiled - The killer, who performed an action — if he did it intentionally, he is not exiled, even at a time when he is not executed, such as when he killed intentionally without forewarning.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:2.hebrew: הם שלא עשו מעשה - אלא דיבור בעלמא, ובמזיד העידו, אינו דין שלא יגלו על המזיד:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:2.english: They, who did not perform an action - Rather, mere speech, and they testified intentionally — is it not logical that they should not be exiled for an intentional [act]?

Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:1.hebrew: ומקשינן לרבי יוחנן והיא הנותנת - המדה הזאת שהבאת לפטרן, היא הנותנת להם חובת גלות. הוא, לפי שעושה מעשה, אם במזיד עשאו אינו גולה, דלא תהוי ליה כפרה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:1.english: And we challenge Rabbi Yochanan: And that [very distinction] provides [the opposite] - This reasoning that you brought to exempt them is [the very thing] that gives them an obligation of exile. He [the murderer], since he performs an action, if he did it intentionally he is not exiled, so that he will not have atonement.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:2.hebrew: הם שלא עשו מעשה יגלו - על זדונן, כי היכי כו':
Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:2.english: They, who did not perform an action, let them be exiled - for their intentional false testimony, so that, etc.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:5:1.hebrew: רמז לעדים זוממין - שלוקין. עדי בן גרושה או עדי גלות, שפטרם הכתוב מדין הזמה, מנין שהן לוקין? ולקמיה פריך: תיפוק ליה מלא תענה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:5:1.english: An allusion to conspiring witnesses - that they are flogged. The witnesses of the son of a divorcée, or the witnesses of exile, whom the verse exempted from the law of conspiracy — from where do we derive that they are flogged? And later the Gemara challenges: Let us derive it from "You shall not bear [false witness]":

Rashi on Makkot 2b:5:2.hebrew: משום דהצדיקו את הצדיק כו' - בתמיה: אי "והצדיקו והרשיעו" בדיינין קאמר, "וצדיק ורשע" בבעלי דינין למה לי? "והצדיקו צדיק כו'" ליכתוב: "כי יהיה ריב בין אנשים ונגשו אל המשפט ושפטום והיה אם בן הכות"; למה הוזכרה כאן צדקת צדיק? וכי כל מקום שהצדיקו ב"ד את הזכאי וחייבו את החייב יש מלקות, דאתא קרא למיתלי מלקות ב"והצדיקו והרשיעו"? אלא על כרחך בעדים משתעי: עדים שקרים שהרשיעו צדיק, ובאו אחרים והזימום, והצדיקו את הנדון שהוא צדיק, והרשיעו את העדים הרשעים, "והיה אם בן הכות את הרשע" — אם הזמה זו בת מלקות היא, שאינו יכול לקיים בה דין הזמה גמורה, כגון בעדי בן גרושה או גלות, והפילו השופט והכהו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:5:2.english: Because "they vindicated the righteous," etc. - [This is said] as a question: If "they vindicated and condemned" refers to judges, and "righteous and wicked" to the litigants, why do I need [it]? As for "they vindicated the righteous," etc., let [the verse] write: "If there is a quarrel between people, and they approach the judgment, and the judges judge them, and it shall be if [the wicked] is deserving of lashes." Why is the vindication of the righteous mentioned here? Is it the case everywhere that when the court vindicates the innocent and condemns the guilty there are lashes, such that the verse comes to link lashes to "they vindicated and condemned"? Rather, you must say that it speaks of witnesses: false witnesses who condemned a righteous person, and others came and conspired against them [i.e., refuted them as conspiring witnesses], and they vindicated the one who was on trial, who is righteous, and condemned the wicked witnesses, "and it shall be if the wicked is deserving of lashes" — if this conspiracy is one that carries lashes, because [the court] cannot carry out against them the full law of conspiring witnesses, such as in the case of witnesses [who testified that someone is] the son of a divorcee, or [who testified to a sentence of] exile — then the judge throws him down and strikes him:

Rashi on Makkot 2b:7:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה מלא תענה - כל עונשי לאוין מלקות, אלא במקום שפירש לך בו עונש. וכאן שאינו יכול לענשן בעונש הכתוב בהן — ילקו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:7:1.english: And let him derive it from “You shall not bear [false witness]” - The punishment for all prohibitions is lashes, except in a place where [the Torah] specified a [different] punishment for you. And here, where one cannot punish them with the punishment written regarding them, they should be flogged.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:7:2.hebrew: לאו שאין בו מעשה אין לוקין עליו - לקמן יליף לה בפרק ג' (דף יג.):
Rashi on Makkot 2b:7:2.english: A prohibition that does not involve an action, one is not flogged for it - Below, [the Gemara] derives this in the third chapter (13a):

Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:1.hebrew: ואין משלמין כופר - אם העידו בשור המועד שהרג את האדם, והוזמו, והיו מחייבין את הבעלים כופר, דכתיב (שמות כ״א:ל׳) אם כופר יושת עליו וגו':
Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:1.english: And they do not pay the ransom - If they testified about a forewarned ox that killed a person, and they were rendered conspiring witnesses, and they would have obligated the owners to pay ransom, [they do not pay it], as it is written (Exodus 21:30): "If a ransom shall be imposed upon him, etc."

Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:2.hebrew: ואין נמכרין - אם העידוהו שגנב, ואין לו מה לשלם, ונגמר דינו לימכר, כדכתיב: ונמכר בגנבתו:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:2.english: And they are not sold - If they testified about him that he stole, and he has nothing with which to pay, and his verdict was finalized to be sold, as it is written: "and he shall be sold for his theft" (Exodus 22:2).

Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:3.hebrew: אין משלמין ע"פ עצמן - אם הוזמו בב"ד, ולא הספיק בעל דין להעמידן בדין על הזמתן עד שברחו ובאו בב"ד אחר, והודו שהוזמו בב"ד פלוני — ולקמן מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:8:3.english: They do not pay based on their own admission - If they were rendered conspiring witnesses in a court, and the opposing litigant did not manage to bring them to judgment over their having been rendered conspiring witnesses before they fled and came to a different court and admitted that they had been rendered conspiring witnesses in such-and-such court — and below [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:9:1.hebrew: כופרא כפרה - לכפר על זה שהרג שורו את האדם. והני לאו בני כפרה נינהו, שלא הרג שורם אדם:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:9:1.english: The ransom is atonement - It is to atone for this one, whose ox killed a person. But these [witnesses] are not subject to atonement, since their ox did not kill a person.

Tosafot on Makkot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל - פי' הקונטרס: כשהרגו אין נהרגין, דין הוא דבאו להרוג ולא הרגו דאין נהרגין. וקשה טובא: חדא, דה"ל למימר, כדאמרינן לקמן (מכות דף ה:): "הרגו אין נהרגין"! ועוד, מאי פריך? שאני הכא, דגלי קרא בהדיא דהבא לסקול ולא סקל דנסקל, בההוא קרא גופיה דחזינן דהסוקל אינו נסקל, כדכתיב: "כאשר זמם" — ולא כאשר עשה; אבל לעולם אימא לך דאית לך שפיר ק"ו דלעיל דלענין חילול, דהא לא גלי קרא בשום מקום דשייך בדבר הזה שיתחלל הזמה! ועוד קשה, דהוה ליה לתרץ דהתם ודאי לא עבדינן ק"ו, משום דא"כ בטלת תורת עדים זוממין לגמרי, ולא משכחת לה "כאשר זמם"; אבל לעיל, דלא בטלת תורת עדים זוממין, שייך שפיר למיעבד ק"ו! לכך פירש ר"ת דה"ק: "ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל" — פירוש: אדם שסוקל חבירו באבנים ומת, דנדון בסייף ולא בסקילה; "הבא ליסקל ולא נסקל" — עדים שמעידין איש פלוני שמחויב סקילה ולא נסקל על ידם, "אינו דין שלא יסקלנו"? והשתא לא בטלת לגמרי, דאיכא לאוקומי קרא ד"ועשיתם כאשר זמם" כשהן מעידין שמחויב שאר מיתות ב"ד שאינו בסקילה. ואפ"ה לא עבדינן האי ק"ו, דהכי קאמר לו לעיל דלא עבדינן ק"ו בכהאי גוונא:
Tosafot on Makkot 2b:1:1.english: "And if one who stones is not stoned" - The commentary of Rashi explained: When they have had the defendant executed they are not executed, is it not logical that when they came to have him executed and did not have him executed, they are not executed? And this is very difficult: First, it should have said the wording, as we say below (Makkot 5b): "If they had him executed, they are not executed"! Furthermore, what is the difficulty the Gemara raises? Here it is different, for the verse explicitly reveals that one who comes to stone and did not stone is himself stoned — in that very verse from which we see that one who stones is not stoned, as it is written: "as he conspired" — and not as he did; whereas I could still say to you that you may well make the kal vachomer above regarding profanation of priesthood, for the verse never revealed anywhere that it applies to this matter that he should become profaned through hazamah! Furthermore, it is difficult that the Gemara should have answered that there we certainly do not make the kal vachomer, because if so, you would abolish the law of conspiring witnesses entirely, and you would never find a case of "as he conspired"; whereas above, where you do not abolish the law of conspiring witnesses, it is well applicable to make the kal vachomer! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that this is what it means: "And if one who stones is not stoned" — meaning: a person who stones his fellow to death with stones, who is judged as a murderer by the sword and not by stoning; "one who comes to have another stoned and he was not stoned" — meaning witnesses who testify that so-and-so is liable to stoning, and he was not stoned through them — "is it not logical that we should not stone him?" And now you do not abolish the law of conspiring witnesses entirely, for one can establish the verse of "and you shall do to him as he conspired" where they testify that he is liable to other court-imposed death penalties that are not by stoning. And even so we do not make this kal vachomer, and thus it says to him that above too we do not make a kal vachomer in such a manner.
